why: ADR-0007 gives the count ('four regions') and the postmortem names two (eu-west, us-east); the names of all four are never listed.
SEV1/SEV2 appear as labels (incident-lead rotation, postmortem severity) but no severity-classification criteria are defined anywhere.
Runbooks give rollback trigger thresholds (2% error rate, p99 400ms) but no availability SLO target for checkout.
ADR-0019 gives sidecar memory per pod (180MB estimated, 310MB measured); no per-node memory figure for the Calder Gateway proxy is stated.
ADR-0007 mentions north-south traffic only in a rejected alternative; both ADRs scope Helix Mesh and Calder Gateway to east-west, and no ingress component is named.
calderctl documents gateway/mesh platform rollbacks and a deploy --version flag, but no procedure for rolling a service back to a previous application version.
calderctl quota set --cpu/--memory exists and the tiers doc says tier does not decide quota; no default quota values for tier 3 (or any tier) are given.
Onboarding says the service-registry name review is 'slower than it looks like it should be' but states no duration.
Onboarding lists team-group membership as a prerequisite; how to create or provision a new team group is never described.
The rota's compensation section covers time off and rotation limits only; no monetary stipend is mentioned.
The retention policy names the role ('data protection lead') as the exception grantor but names no person.
ADR-0007 says a platform exception exists and expires after 90 days; the request procedure and the approver are not stated.
The calderctl reference marks which commands write and lists exit codes, but says nothing about audit logging or where an audit trail lives.
One postmortem exists as an artifact, but no publication deadline and no postmortem template are documented.
Payments appears as a tier 1 revenue-path service and as checkout's dependency; no owning team is named.
ADR-0019 describes Calder Gateway's placement, mTLS and policy carry-over; no protocol support (HTTP/3, gRPC streaming) is discussed.
The gateway runbook mandates --max-surge 1 for node-by-node reverts but gives no connection-draining timeout.
The retention policy mentions a 35-day backup window and expiry-based deletion; no restore procedure or recovery-time expectation appears.
The policy states a verified deletion request must complete within 30 days across five store types, but not how a request is submitted or verified.
Kubernetes is implied only by an admission controller and pods/nodes; no cluster version or upgrade cadence is given.
